main_text.p: eatorum nihil aliud est, quàm à morte, peccati poenâ, plena & perpetua libe-ratio.

2. In cognitione sic fit collatio: Sic-ut sacrificiis illis peractis, is, pro quo victima offerebatur, iam de divina erga se benignitate & placatione amplius dubitare non poterat, & sibi delictum suum condonatum, pro certo habe-bat: Sic morte ([illegible, ~7 letters])Christi, seu supplicio ejus peracto, nemo est, qui, Deum nos supremâ caritate complexum fuisse, non agnoscat, eumque erga nos placatissimum non videat, qui dile-ctissimum Filium suum, ut nobis ad aeternam salutem, eâ viâ, quam ipse ad potentiam & gloriam suam patefaci-endam sapientissimè elegit, Dux & Præcursor esset, tantis malis objecerit; & jam sibi universa delicta, ipsius summâ liberalitate, condonata esse (iis tamen conditionibus acceptis, quas ipse æquissimas in condonatione adscripsit) pro certo non habeat.Collatio[illegible, ~9 letters]
II. Imparitèr verò conferunt Christi mortem, cum victimis legalibus, cùmCollatio in[?]par. prima

page.notes: The first letter of the opening line "eatorum" is cut off by the scan edge; left as printed. The Greek parenthetical after "Sic morte" is too faint to read, so it is marked illegible. The marginal notes at the top right are only partly legible; the second one is unreadable. A stray bullet mark stands in the right margin beside "suum" and is not printed text. The word "cùm" at the foot is a catchword, not part of the paragraph. The running head shows "CAP. V. SECT. III." with a small mark beside it, which is not transcribed.
